title: At someone's home
goal: Visit a friend's family and feel at ease: arrive and greet their parents, accept and refuse food the Gujarati way, offer to help, stay the night, say goodbye properly, and talk about how things used to be.
intro:
Sooner or later a Gujarati friend will say **ઘરે આવ ને, મમ્મી જમાડશે** — 'come over, Mum will feed you'. Gujarati homes are famously hospitable, and a visit has its own little script: shoes off at the door, **જય શ્રી કૃષ્ણ** to the parents, a first 'no' to food that nobody believes, the host's **આગ્રહ** (insisting), and a long goodbye at the door.

This unit gives you that script: offering and declining politely, 'shall I…?' with **દઉં** and **લઉં**, and the **'used to'** form, because sitting on the swing after dinner, someone always starts with **પહેલાં તો અમે…** 'we used to…'.

grammar.title: 'Used to': જતો, જતો હતો
grammar.body:
For things that happened **regularly in the past** Gujarati uses the **-તો** form of the verb — the same form you know from negatives like **નથી જતો**. You can use it alone or add **હતો**; both mean 'used to':

નાનપણમાં હું દર ઉનાળે મામાને ત્યાં **જતો** 'as a child I used to go to my uncle's every summer'
= નાનપણમાં હું દર ઉનાળે મામાને ત્યાં **જતો હતો**

The -તો form agrees with the **subject**, like an adjective:

**-તો** man · **-તી** woman · **-તું** neuter
**-તા** men, a mixed group, or one person you respect (દાદા, પપ્પા)
**-તાં** a mixed group, children, or a respected woman (દાદી, મમ્મી in careful speech)

With હતો both parts agree: મમ્મી **બનાવતી હતી**, દાદા **કહેતા હતા**.

**Negative:** **નહોતો** + -તો: **હું ચા નહોતો પીતો** 'I didn't use to drink tea'. Contrast with now using **હવે** or **આજકાલ**: પહેલાં હું ચા નહોતો પીતો, **હવે** રોજ પીઉં છું.

For habits you can also say **મને … -વાની ટેવ હતી** 'I was in the habit of…'.

**The trap:** this form never takes the ergative, even with verbs like ખાવું, પીવું, કરવું: say **હું** ચા પીતો, never 'મેં ચા પીતો'. The ergative is only for the one-off past (મેં ચા **પીધી** 'I drank tea').

grammar.title: Offering, insisting and saying no politely
grammar.body:
Gujarati hospitality runs on **આગ્રહ** — insisting. The host offers, the guest says no, the host insists, and the guest takes 'just a little'. Knowing the lines makes it easy.

**Offering:** **લો ને / લે ને** ('do have'), **થોડું વધારે લો**, **ચાખી જુઓ** ('try it'), **એક તો લો!** ('at least one!'), **સંકોચ ના રાખો**.

**Saying no, nicely:** never a bare ના. Say **ના ના, બસ**, give a reason — **હું ધરાઈ ગયો / ગઈ** 'I'm full', **હમણાં જ જમીને આવ્યો** 'I've just eaten' — and praise the food: **બહુ સરસ બન્યું છે**.

**Giving in:** **સારું, થોડુંક જ**, **અડધી જ આપો** 'just half'.

**Turning down help:** the host says **રહેવા દો / રહેવા દે** 'leave it', **તમે તો મહેમાન છો** 'you're a guest'.

**Food you like** is **ભાવે**, not just ગમે: **મને કઢી બહુ ભાવે છે**.

**The trap:** the first ના is expected and not taken seriously — if you really want more, a quiet **હા, થોડું** is fine; if you really don't, say it twice, with a reason and a smile. Covering your plate with your hand is the clear final 'no'.

examples.en: Do have a bit more dal!

examples.native: ના ના, ખરેખર બસ. હું ધરાઈ ગઈ.
examples.roman: nā nā, kharekhar bas. huṃ dharāī gaī.
examples.en: No, no, honestly, that's enough. I'm full. (woman)

examples.roman: ek roṭlī to levī j paḍshe!
examples.en: You've got to have at least one more roti!

examples.en: At least try it, Mum made it herself.

grammar.title: Shall I…? with દઉં and લઉં
grammar.body:
You know the subjunctive for 'shall I?' (unit 18): **હું કરું?** In real offers Gujaratis nearly always add a helper verb after the -ઈ form:

**-ઈ દેવું** — doing it **for someone else**: **વાસણ ધોઈ દઉં?** 'shall I wash the dishes (for you)?'
**-ઈ લેવું** — doing it **for yourself**, or just getting it done: **પાણી લઈ લઉં?** 'may I help myself to water?'

The subjunctive of દેવું and લેવું is irregular:

હું **દઉં** · તું **દે** · એ **દે** · અમે / આપણે **દઈએ** · તમે **દો** · એ લોકો **દે**
હું **લઉં** · તું **લે** · એ **લે** · અમે / આપણે **લઈએ** · તમે **લો** · એ લોકો **લે**

Add **છું** and it becomes a promise: **હું કરી દઉં છું** 'I'll do it (right now)'.

To ask what the **house rule** is, use **-વાનું છે?** 'is one supposed to…?': **ચંપલ બહાર ઉતારવાનાં છે?** 'are shoes to be left outside?', or the impersonal **-આય**: **અહીં બેસાય?** 'is it OK to sit here?'

**The trap:** 'shall I' is never the future: **હું કરીશ?** means 'will I do it?'. And it's **દઉં** and **લઉં**, not 'દેઉં' or 'લેઉં'.

examples.en: Can I charge my phone here?
Shall I make you some tea?

examples.native: હું જાતે લઈ લઉં છું, તમે બેસો.
examples.roman: huṃ jāte laī lauṃ chhuṃ, tame beso.
examples.en: I'll help myself, you sit down.
Should I leave my shoes outside?

culture: Never arrive empty-handed: a box of sweets or some fruit is normal. Shoes come off at the door, and you greet your friend's parents as **આન્ટી / અંકલ** (or **માસી / કાકા**) with **જય શ્રી કૃષ્ણ** or **નમસ્તે**, always with **તમે**; at festivals younger people may touch elders' feet (**પગે લાગવું**). Whatever time you arrive you'll be offered at least tea and a snack, and at mealtimes the host keeps serving: the first 'no' is part of the ritual, praise is expected, and a hand over the plate is the final word. Many families are vegetarian, some don't eat onion and garlic (Jain households), and it's polite not to bring meat or eggs into the house. After the meal comes **મુખવાસ**, and often a chat on the **હીંચકો**. Leaving takes time: guests say **ચાલો, રજા લઉં** or simply **આવું છું** ('I'll come again') rather than 'I'm going', hosts answer **આવજો** and walk you to the door or the lift. In the diaspora the same script holds — in Leicester or New Jersey any older Gujarati woman is 'aunty', and you'll still be told **જમીને જ જજો!**

tip.title: Greeting the family
tip.body:
- Your friend's parents are **આન્ટી / અંકલ** (or **માસી / કાકા**): greet them with **જય શ્રી કૃષ્ણ** or **નમસ્તે** and use **તમે**.
- With your friend, stay with **તું**.
- Shoes come off at the door: **ચંપલ ક્યાં ઉતારું?** — the bare verb **ઉતારું** means 'shall I…?'.

lessons.title: At the table: yes, no and "just a little"

tip.title: Offering and saying no
tip.body:
- Offer with **લો ને / લે ને**, **ચાખી જુઓ**, **સંકોચ ના રાખો**.
- Say no softly, with a reason: **ના ના, બસ, હું ધરાઈ ગયો / ગઈ**.
- Give in with **સારું, થોડુંક જ**.
- Food you like **ભાવે**: મને કઢી **ભાવે છે**, મને તીખું નથી **ભાવતું**.

new: ના ના, બસ, હું ધરાઈ ગયો.

sentences.en: I really love kadhi.
Do you like khichdi?
I don't like spicy food.
I'm full, aunty. (woman)

sentences.roman: ānṭī, dāḷ bahu svādiṣṭ banī chhe!

Don't hold back, eat properly. (informal)
That's it, no more, honestly.

tip.title: 'Used to': જતો, જતો હતો
tip.body:
- Regular past habits use the **-તો** form, alone or with **હતો**: હું ત્યાં **જતો** / **જતો હતો**.
- It agrees with the subject: **-તો / -તી / -તું / -તા / -તાં**.
- No ergative: **હું** ચા પીતો (not 'મેં').
- Contrast with now: પહેલાં … , **હવે / આજકાલ** …

sentences.native: નાનપણમાં અમે આખો દિવસ બહાર રમતાં.
sentences.roman: nānpaṇmāṃ ame ākho divas bahār ramtāṃ.
sentences.en: As kids we used to play outside all day.

sentences.roman: ame dar ravivāre dādāne ghare jatā.

sentences.native: પહેલાં હું રોજ ચા પીતો, હવે કૉફી પીઉં છું.

sentences.native: પહેલાં હું બહુ બહાર જમતો, આજકાલ ઘરે જ જમું છું.

tip.title: Shall I…? દઉં and લઉં
tip.body:
- Offer to do something **for them** with **-ઈ દઉં?**: વાસણ **ધોઈ દઉં?**
- Do something **for yourself** with **-ઈ લઉં?**: પાણી **લઈ લઉં?**
- Forms: હું **દઉં / લઉં**, આપણે **દઈએ / લઈએ**, તમે **દો / લો**.
- Never the future: 'હું કરીશ?' means 'will I?'.

sentences.en: Shall I do the dishes?
Aunty, shall I make the rotis?
Leave it, you're our guest!
Can I help myself to some water?

sentences.native: સાવરણી આપ, ચાલ આપણે સાથે ઘર સાફ કરી દઈએ.
sentences.roman: sāvarṇī āp, chāl āpaṇe sāthe ghar sāf karī daīe.
sentences.en: Pass me the broom, come on, let's clean the house together.

sentences.native: પોતું હું કરી દઉં છું, તું આરામ કર.
sentences.roman: potuṃ huṃ karī dauṃ chhuṃ, tuṃ ārām kar.
sentences.en: I'll do the mopping, you have a rest.
Shall I sit here?

sentences.native: અમારા ઘરમાં નિયમ છે કે બધા સાથે જમે.
sentences.roman: amārā gharmāṃ niyam chhe ke badhā sāthe jame.
sentences.en: The rule in our house is that everyone eats together.
Is it OK to go into the kitchen with shoes on?
Everyone helps with the housework.

new: આજે રાત્રે અહીં જ રોકાઈ જા.
તમને તકલીફ તો નહીં પડે ને?

sentences.roman: moḍuṃ thaī gayuṃ chhe, āje ahīṃ j rokāī jāo.

sentences.native: હું તારા માટે ગાદલું પાથરી દઉં છું.
sentences.roman: huṃ tārā māṭe gādluṃ pātharī dauṃ chhuṃ.
sentences.en: I'll put a mattress down for you.

sentences.native: રાત્રે ઠંડી લાગે તો ધાબળો કબાટમાં છે.

sentences.native: ના, ચાદર બસ છે, ગરમી છે.
sentences.roman: nā, chādar bas chhe, garmī chhe.

sentences.native: બાથરૂમમાં ગરમ પાણી ક્યારે આવે છે?

sentences.native: મને ગમે ત્યાં ઊંઘ આવી જાય છે.
sentences.roman: mane game tyāṃ ūṃgh āvī jāy chhe.
sentences.en: I can sleep anywhere.

sentences.native: હું નીચે ગાદલા પર સૂઈ જઈશ, કોઈ વાંધો નહીં.

sentences.native: સવારે ચા કેટલા વાગ્યે પીઓ છો?
sentences.roman: savāre chā keṭlā vāgye pīo chho?

tip.title: Leaving, the Gujarati way
tip.body:
- Take your leave with **ચાલો, હવે રજા લઉં** — not a blunt 'I'm going'.
- On the way out Gujaratis say **આવું છું** 'I'll come (again)' rather than જાઉં છું, and hosts answer **આવજો**.
- Thank them: **મહેમાનગતિ માટે આભાર**.
tip.pattern: ચાલો, રજા લઉં · આવું છું · આવજો

sentences.en: Right, we should get going now.

sentences.en: Say Jai Shri Krishna to everyone at home.

sentences.roman: are, hajī to sāt vāgyā chhe!
sentences.en: Hey, it's only seven!

It was really lovely, see you again.
